title: O Father, — Draw Us After Thee
description: O Father, — Draw Us After Thee in Tonic Solfa to MELITA, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 612 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Invocation of our Father's Presence”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre, six lines (8.8.8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELITA; any other Long Metre, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: O Fa-ther, draw us af-ter thee! So shall we run and nev-er tire; Thy pre-sence still our com-fort be, Our hope, our joy, our sole de-sire; Thy Spir-it grant; for nei-ther fear Nor sin can come, while that is here.

lines: O Father, — draw us after thee!
So shall we run and never tire;
Thy presence still our comfort be,
Our hope, our joy, our sole desire;
Thy Spirit grant; — for neither fear
Nor sin can come, while that is here.
Before these beating hearts did move,
Ever with us may they abide,
And close us in on every side.
In suffering be thy love our peace;
In weakness be thy love our power;
And when the storms of life shall cease,
O God! in that important hour,
In death as life be thou our guide,
And bear us through death's whelming tide.

credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to MELITA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
